page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, set right of centre, with no marginal notes. A handwritten mark sits at top left and is left out. The right edge of the scan cuts into the last letters of some lines. Running head at top, page number 430 with it. Text ends with a catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: sensu populi sibi constituit : Et appellatur alias jus municipale, seu statutum, vulgo Wilkhür / Weichbild/oder Stattrecht.
Quis autem possit condere statuta, dicit Schneidevvinus ad §.jus autem civil.inst.hoc titulo.

head.i: Quid est Jus Civile privatum non scriptum?

main_text.p: Est quod usus approbavit. Nam diuturni mores, consensu utentium comprobati, legem imitantur. §. sine scripto, inst. cod. Et dicitur Consuetudo Specialis. Quomodo autem consuetudo introducatur, docet Schneidevvinus hic.

Naturalia quidem jura, quæ apud omnes gentes peræque observantur. Divina quadam providentia constituta, semper firma atque immutabilia permanent. Ea vero quæ ipsa sibi quæque civitas constituit sæpe mutari solent, vel tacito consensu populi, vel alia postea lege lata.§.sed natural.inst.eod.

Omne jus, quo utimur, vel ad personas pertinet, (quibus jus redditur) vel ad res (de quibus jus redditur) vel ad actiones (per quas jus redditur.) Et prius de personis videamus. Nam parum est jus nosse, si personæ, quarum causa constitutum est, ignorentur. §.final.inst.eod. Vide Vvesenbecium[?] super institut.
main_text.head: QUIS EST TERTIUS Titulus?
De Jure Personarum. Vom Recht der Personen.
main_text.p: Summa divisio personarum hæc est, quod omnes homines aut liberi sunt, aut servi. in princ.inst.eod. l.3. de statu hominum..

page.notes: Right edge of the scan cuts off the last letters of several lines (e.g. "constituit", "consensu", "introducatur"); those words are read from the visible parts. "Vvesenbecium" is doubtful: the second letter could be "e" or "c". The black-letter words "Wilkhür", "Weichbild/oder Stattrecht", "Vom Recht" and "der Personen." are read from the scan and may be imperfect. The title "QUIS EST TERTIUS" is an ordinal without a Roman numeral, so no caput number is given. The handwritten mark at top left is omitted.
